Independently re-derived the pure arithmetic/lattice facts in GC-6 with fresh code and different methods, and they check out: (1) Sugawara central charges c(SU(3)_2)=16/5, c((G2)_1)=14/5, sum=6=c((E6)_1)=78/13, confirmed exactly with an independent Fraction computation. (3) The 27-coset minimal-norm claim (norm^2=4/3, multiplicity 27) was reproduced independently from the abstract Cartan-matrix construction with a brute-force (non-Fincke-Pohst) box search once the box was widened enough to avoid truncation artifacts (initial box -3..3 under-counted at 24; -6..6 gave exactly 27). (4) The B672 rewrite arithmetic (2/5-5/12=-1/60, 3/5-5/12=11/60) is correct fraction arithmetic, and -1/60, 11/60 are indeed the standard Lee-Yang/(2,5)-minimal-model leading exponents (Rocha-Caridi h-c/24 with c=-22/5, h=0,-1/5) — a genuine, well-known RR/(2,5)-model correspondence, not fabricated.

However, the headline's two central claims outrun what the computation establishes, so the claim as stated is refuted:

(a) "provably ABSENT from every banked object-side series" is a universal quantifier that the code never tests. The script only builds a two-element proxy set object_exps = {0} ∪ {2/5,3/5} (comment: B672's doublet is asserted, not demonstrated, to be "the ONLY banked object-side q-series family") and checks that against {3/4,5/12}. No enumeration of the repo's actual banked object-side series (WRT/Habiro q-series across B854, B866, cusp-shape series, other campaigns) was performed, so "every" is unsupported — it is a claim about one hand-picked representative, not a survey.

(b) The "partially PRESENT" claim rests on matching a q-series prefactor exponent from an unrelated construction (B672's Y^(5) grading, whose associated chiral algebra when written as Lee-Yang-character × η^10 has total central charge 28/5, matching neither c=6 nor the SU(3)_2×G2_1 pair) to Sugawara conformal weights h=2/5, h=3/5 of specific WZW primaries. These are different kinds of quantities (a q-series overall power vs. h in q^(h-c/24)) with no established bridge map between them, and the whole ambient program is saturated with denominator-5/golden-ratio structures, so a match on {2/5,3/5} carries little discriminating power — it reads as a coincidental fraction match dressed as "the RR/Fibonacci hallmark firing," not a computed instance of an actual embedding.

Net: the sub-computations are numerically sound (verified independently), but the claim's scope (a "provable" absence-everywhere plus a meaningful partial-presence signal) is not supported by what was actually computed — an overreach on both the negative and positive halves of the headline.

Instrument defect on the quantifier, which is load-bearing for the headline. The headline asserts a UNIVERSAL claim -- the (E6)_1 exponent signature {3/4,5/12} is "provably ABSENT from every banked object-side series" -- but the code never enumerates or iterates over "every banked object-side series." It constructs exactly one hand-assembled set, `object_exps = {Fr(0)} | doublet_exps` = {0, 2/5, 3/5} (a manual union of "the WRT/index-type series has integer exponents" plus the single B672 doublet's two exponents), and tests only that one set's intersection with {3/4,5/12}. That is a per-point check on one representative combination, not a proof over the full banked-series inventory (other WRT levels m, other cusps, other banked q-series elsewhere in the repo besides B672's doublet are never touched by this script). So the "provably ABSENT from every ... series" language in the headline is not what was computed; at most the run supports "absent from the one hand-picked combined set tested." This is exactly the per-point-vs-generic-vs-all mismatch the lens calls out, and it directly undercuts the strongest half of the split verdict (the E6-absence claim).

Secondary, compounding defect in the two-sided control: the BITE/exclusion target chosen to demonstrate the instrument "can exclude a deliberately-absent target" is (E8)_1 with exponent class {2/3} (denominator 3), tested against an object set whose only nonzero denominators are 5 (2/5, 3/5). Because the candidate exponent-sets here are tiny (2-3 rational values each) and the chosen negative control has a structurally different denominator from the start, the "ABSENT" result for (E8)_1 is guaranteed by construction and carries almost no discriminating power -- it doesn't show the instrument can catch a near-miss (e.g. a denominator-5 competitor that isn't actually the same physics), only that it can distinguish two sets with different denominators, which is close to tautological. A genuine two-sided control needs a deliberately-absent target that is a plausible confusable, not an arithmetically distant one; as run, the exclusion side does not certify that the "ABSENT" verdict against (E6)_1 carries real discriminating content.

The positive-control arithmetic (Kashaev growth recovering Vol; the E6 lattice character construction; the doublet/split-pair exponent match) is legitimate exact/converging computation and is not itself in question. But because the headline's "provably ABSENT from every banked object-side series" rests on an instrument that (a) checks one hand-built set rather than the stated universal class, and (b) pairs that with a BITE control too weak to certify the check's discriminating power, the verdict as stated is not supported by the computation shown and should be refuted under this lens.
